tasks.short: Observe paving distribution and adjust material placement

steps.what: Observe distribution of paving material and identify low spots
Adjust machine settings or material flow for the observed distribution
outputs: adjusted paving settings and material flow

steps.what: Indicate the low spots where workers must add material
inputs: adjusted paving settings and material flow
outputs: low-spot directions understood by paving crew

tasks.design: Keep visual observation, local adjustments and crew directions with the operator. Existing {OPS_SYSTEM} paving controls may assist material flow, but their normal runtime is not saved operator time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Distribution varies with the material, substrate and moving equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing controls can assist operation; no additional software saving is established here.
tasks.still_hard: Detect and correct local defects while people work near the equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Connect visual conditions to safe adjustments and clear directions.

ambition.what: Maintain paving quality and situational awareness.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: paving equipment controls assist material placement, while operators observe conditions and direct local corrections.

assumptions: Boundary explicitly includes settings writes and communication as separate actions. It does not hide a report in observation: this statement has no report deliverable. Any separately required quality log must be assessed separately.
OTHER means physical paving equipment and road bed; OPS_SYSTEM means its existing control interface. No camera, autonomous control or sensor installation is assumed.
Native material-flow controls must be inspected before proposing anything. No extra saving follows merely from keeping their existing automation running.
Shares are provisional estimates of this work, independent of the prompt means prior. B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0.
unknowns: Whether local corrections still require the operator despite automatic flow control
research_questions: Observe a paving pass and separate screen adjustments from observation and crew directions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No measured or specified mechanism reduces these live observation, adjustment or communication actions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate truck dumping at the paver

steps.what: Confirm the next truck's identity, load and arrival status with dispatch
inputs: existing dispatch load and arrival records
outputs: confirmed next truck and load status

steps.what: Check that the dumping zone and paver are ready for the approaching truck
inputs: confirmed next truck and load status

steps.what: Signal the truck driver to approach, dump, pause and leave as conditions require

tasks.design: Show current dispatch load and arrival status in {OPS_SYSTEM} so the operator can confirm the next truck with fewer routine calls. Readiness checks and all approach, dump and departure signals stay with the operator at the paving site.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dispatch information may require a call while the operator is coordinating equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: A native dispatch view can expose existing load status without automating vehicle movement.
tasks.still_hard: A record cannot establish that the immediate dumping zone is safe.
tasks.human_edge: Control the live interaction between driver, paver and crew.

ambition.what: Reduce routine status checking while preserving live dumping control.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; dispatch visibility and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: dispatch records can expose truck and load status while local workers retain vehicle-movement decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is coordinating truck dumping, including status confirmation, readiness and live signals; no unload report is implied or omitted from a conversation step.

Existing dispatch producer records truck ID, job ID, load material and quantity, departure time, reported ETA/status and status timestamp for normal dispatch. The view reads those existing fields. No new driver entry or tracking is assumed; stale or missing status falls back to the current call in s1.

Configure native dispatch visibility first. The central scenario requires real current phone confirmation and usable dispatch data for 40% of that effort. If a view already exists, do not claim a new saving. No reduction in readiness checks or driver signals.
No machine sends or vehicle-control commits occur. Direct live driver signals are ordinary operator decisions, not automated actions requiring a version gate.
Provisional shares come from the coordination sequence, not the means prior. B=100, R=94, gross=6; focal incremental=0.5; net=5.5.
unknowns: Availability and freshness of existing dispatch records
research_questions: Compare dispatch status timestamps with actual truck arrivals and count avoidable routine calls.

already_counted.description: Read current status and resolve stale or missing dispatch data

incremental.description: Check status-view failures and contact dispatch when the view becomes unreliable

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: native visibility already covers status confirmation, so no deployment. High: usable records avoid six hours of calls, but another 1.5 hours of stale-status checks beyond central and 0.5 hours of upkeep leave four.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Live paving and vehicle coordination remain operator work; existing dispatch data may reduce routine status calls.
reach: Truck driver: agree clear live dumping signals
skills_to_grow: Use equipment controls with direct site observation
role.ambitious_version: A paving operator with timely load information who retains control of material placement and truck interaction.
